paper.title_en: Gravitational-wave propagation constraints on the dynamical Barbero--Immirzi field from GWTC-3 dark sirens
paper.abstract_en: The Barbero--Immirzi (BI) parameter, originally a constant in the Holst term of first-order gravity, can be promoted to a dynamical scalar field $γ(x)$, coupled to torsion in Einstein--Cartan theory. We derive the effective gravitational-wave (GW) propagation equation in this framework, identifying an extra friction term $Γ_{\mathrm{BI}}\proptoξ_{\mathrm{BI}}H$ induced by the BI scalar stress-energy. Using the Belgacem--Maggiore parameterisation to connect this to the GW luminosity distance, we confront the prediction with the LIGO--Virgo--KAGRA GWTC-3 dark-siren constraint $Ξ_{0}=1.2^{+0.7}_{-0.7}$. Translating the published posterior into a conservative bound yields $|ξ_{\mathrm{BI}}|\lesssim 2.0$ (90\% CL). Within the torsion-BI effective description, this gives a model-dependent constraint on the combination $g_{γT}^{2}γ_{\mathrm{dyn}}$. For $g_{γT}\sim\mathcal{O}(1)$ and the benchmark normalisation $C=1$, this corresponds to a characteristic scale $γ_{\mathrm{dyn}}\lesssim\mathcal{O}(10^{-8})$, which should be regarded as a benchmark realisation rather than a direct measurement of the microscopic BI-field amplitude. This constraint probes a different physical sector from the terahertz torsion-wave bound $γ\lesssim 10^{-58}$ and does not rely on torsion-wave excitation. Our result indicates that current GW data already permit a nontrivial test of quantum-gravity-inspired torsion scenarios.
